title: Infectious and non-infectious diseases
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:23Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers only non-infectious diseases at Year 12 depth (chromosomes, mutations, tumours, inherited conditions), while the new point is a Stage 5 introduction contrasting infectious diseases spreading via pathogens with non-infectious ones and how healthy habits lower risk, so it is a different and shallower idea.

draft.title: Infectious and non-infectious diseases
card: a disease caused by a pathogen, such as a bacterium or virus. It can spread from one person to another.
a disease that is not caused by a pathogen and cannot spread between people. Heart disease and type 2 diabetes are examples.
Non-infectious diseases can come from genes, lifestyle or the environment, or a mix of these. Lifestyle means habits such as diet, exercise and smoking.
Healthy habits, such as regular exercise and a balanced diet, can lower the risk of some non-infectious diseases. They do not remove the risk completely.
draft.remember: Infectious diseases come from pathogens and can spread. Non-infectious diseases do not, and healthy habits can lower their risk.

a.q: What is the main difference between an infectious and a non-infectious disease?
opts: Infectious diseases are caused by pathogens
Infectious diseases are caused by lifestyle choices
Non-infectious diseases are caused by pathogens
a.why: An infectious disease is caused by a pathogen, which is why it can spread. Non-infectious diseases are not caused by pathogens, so they do not pass from person to person.
a.clue: Think about what causes each type, and whether it can spread.

b.q: Sam's grandfather has type 2 diabetes. His classmate Lily has the flu. Which statement about their illnesses is correct?
opts: Lily's flu can spread to others, but diabetes cannot
Sam's grandfather's diabetes can spread to others
Neither illness can spread, as both are caused by lifestyle
Both illnesses can spread, as both can run in families
b.why: Flu is caused by a virus, so it is infectious and can spread. Type 2 diabetes is non-infectious: genes and lifestyle can play a part, but no pathogen causes it. Running in a family does not make a disease infectious.
b.clue: Ask whether a pathogen causes each illness.

a.best: Infectious diseases are caused by pathogens

b.best: Lily's flu can spread to others, but diabetes cannot
